evidence.quote: Today, the FOMC raised our policy interest rate by 75 basis points.
incoming data since our last meeting suggest that the ultimate level of interest rates will be higher than previously expected.
It's very premature, in my view, to think about or be talking about pausing our rate hike. We have a ways to go.
And the recent inflation data again have come in higher than expected. Price pressures remain evident across a broad range of goods and services.
the labor market remains extremely tight, with the unemployment rate at a 50-year low, job vacancies still very high, and wage growth elevated.
we want to be sure that we don't make the mistake of either failing to tighten enough or loosening policy too soon.

parsed.rationale: The Chair announces another 75 bp hike, signals ongoing increases to a terminal rate higher than previously expected, and calls talk of pausing very premature, citing persistent inflation and a very tight labor market. Signals of a possible slower pace are explicitly subordinated to how high and how long rates stay restrictive, leaving the net message strongly hawkish.
